thread:
maria: heads up — after the 1.3.0 python-sdk release i'm seeing connection explosions during our load test. sockets pile up and we hit OOM/file-descriptor limits. :grimacing:

sam: ugh, did you pin any config? we changed default connector behavior in 1.3.0 to be more optimistic about keepalives.

maria: nope, no special config. simple usage:

maria: ```py
from redwood import RedwoodAsyncClient

client = RedwoodAsyncClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))

async def do_work(i):
    await client.generate(prompt=f"hello {i}")

# launched 500 tasks concurrently
await asyncio.gather(*(do_work(i) for i in range(500)))
```

maria: after a few hundred requests fd usage shoots up to 10k on the test runner. errors look like: 

maria: ```
OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/asyncio/tasks.py", line 123, in wait
ConnectionResetError: Connection reset by peer
```

kevin: can you repro with a single long-lived client + context manager? we recommend reusing the client but i want to confirm it's not created per-task.

maria: yes, that's a single global client. i double-checked.

olivia: is this only on async or also sync?

maria: async only so far. sync runner looked stable.

sam: likely the aiohttp TCPConnector defaults changed. we added some heuristics to favor parallelism but didn't set connection limits. that can blow up for high concurrency.

kevin: quick mitigation — throttle concurrency with a semaphore in userland or set connector limits. maria, can you try patching client.session._connector.limit = 100 and see? (hacky but fast repro)

maria: tried manually mutating, limit helped but then we saw huge number of TCP TIME_WAIT sockets. increasing keepalive didn't help.

olivia: log snippet from the repro: 

olivia: ```
INFO 2026-06-01 18:02:11 root: starting 500 tasks
WARNING 2026-06-01 18:02:12 httpx._client: opening new connection to api.redwood.ai
ERROR 2026-06-01 18:02:15 OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files
```

maria: workaround we used: single worker with bounded queue + backoff. not great though.

sam: we should treat as P1 for the SDK stable branch. user-facing regressions on default install are bad.

kevin: proposed action items:
- add config to RedwoodAsyncClient to accept a custom aiohttp/TCPConnector or explicit connection limits (limit_per_host, limit)
- expose keepalive and ttl vals and doc recommended defaults for high concurrency
- add example in samples/async_pooling_demo showing correct pattern with semaphores and connector config
- add telemetry to track open sockets/connector stats in DEBUG logs

maria: feature request: please make it easy to use a shared connector across processes in gunicorn/uvicorn setups. currently session lifecycle is tied to client object which sometimes gets GC'd oddly.

sam: agreed. we should also add explicit .close() and contextmanager examples everywhere. i can add a deprecation-safe fix to ensure finalizer doesn't spawn new connectors once shutdown started.

olivia: typing bug: when using from typing import TypedDict for request shapes, AsyncClient.request doesn't type-check in mypy. we lost some generics in 1.3.0. can we restore AsyncClient[T] generics?

kevin: noted. SDK parity is important — sync/async should mirror types. add to PR checklist.

maria: also saw odd retry behavior: when connector fails with ConnectionResetError the SDK starts creating new sessions to retry instead of reusing existing connection pool. that amplifies the fd leak.

sam: that's likely the bug — retry wrapper recreates client internals on error. i'll trace that.

ci-bot: CI pipeline: py-sdk-tests/async-suite failing on test_pool_limits — 17 failing, 2 flaky. https://ci.redwood/c/1234

kevin: thanks, ci-bot. i'll pick this up after stand. plan for 1.3.1 hotfix: revert the connector heuristic and add explicit config knobs.

maria: would love a temporary flag env REDWOOD_AIO_LIMIT to set connector limit via env for quick rollouts.

sam: good idea. i'll add env override + docs.

olivia: for long term, we should ship a small sample app in examples/async/ that demonstrates recommended concurrency patterns:
- share single client across lifespan
- pass custom TCPConnector(limit_per_host=...)
- use asyncio.Semaphore for in-flight requests
- graceful close on shutdown hooks (uvicorn lifespan events)

maria: thanks. adding test matrix items: stress test with 1k coroutines against local mock, ensure fd stays bounded.

kevin: i'll open an issue and a draft PR today. tagging @sam for the connector changes and @olivia for typing fixes.

sam: assign to me. will also add release note about sdk behavior change. :thumbsup:

maria: appreciate it — saving customers from midnight outages. :pray:

kevin: update: created GH issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/412 and draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/419

maria: verified 1.3.1-alpha with local patch — fd stays under 300 for 500 concurrent tasks. will run longer soak tomorrow and report.

olivia: great, keep us posted. i'll prep typing tests for mypy in the CI matrix.
